items.translation: we (informal), people in general, someone, one — always with a 3rd person singular verb
items.exampleFr: On va au cinéma. En France, on dîne tard. On frappe à la porte.
items.exampleEn: We are going to the cinema. In France, people dine late. Someone is knocking at the door.

items.translation: The same pronoun with l' added for the sound, in careful writing
items.exampleFr: C'est un pays où l'on mange bien.
items.exampleEn: It is a country where one eats well.

items.translation: After et, ou, où, que, si, lorsque — to avoid two vowels meeting, or the sound of “qu'on”
items.exampleFr: Si l'on veut. Ce que l'on dit.
items.exampleEn: If one wishes. What people say.

items.translation: Not at the start of a sentence in ordinary prose, and not before a word starting with l
When on means nous, the participle or adjective may take the plural

items.prompt: In “On frappe à la porte”, on means…

items.explain: Avoid l'on before a word that starts with l.
